lines.text: A customer writes: “I paid on the 20th, here's my screenshot.” Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Nebius Token Factory, reads the photo. The payment ledger has no payment at that time.
The reply asks politely. The customer answers: “Sorry, it was the 19th.” Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the answer, and the agent checks the ledger again. Now it matches.
The money chain shows where it really stopped: the credits arrived, the email never did. The reply is rewritten, and the fix waits for the seller to approve.
Why a model at all? On this card alert, free OCR with rules grabs two hundred eighty-eight thousand three hundred won: the card bill. Nemotron picks the payment to the shop.
On sixteen held-out phone photos made by a separate agent, Nemotron read the payment right and reached the right verdict on fourteen. Free OCR with rules, three.
A genuine payment goes straight through: same amount, within ten minutes.
Messages are messy too. Two addresses: the account is his wife's, but he paid with his own.
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the message: who is writing, what they claim, which records to look up. Addresses are masked before the model sees them, and anything the message doesn't say is dropped.
A simple rule would grab the first address and find nothing.
A verifier, not the model, walks the chain. The order was saved under a typo, exmaple dot com, and the mail bounced.
Every call is on screen: which Nemotron did which job, the time, the tokens and the cost. Ultra re-reads when the first reading is unsure, which on Korean threads was most of the time.
Approve, and the fix runs. On the public demo, only your own copy of the data changes.
Ask for someone else's order, and it is not read. And when nothing was charged, it says so. Nothing is broken. You were never charged.
On twenty-two Korean-heavy messages, Nemotron found who was writing in twenty; rules alone, sixteen. When it could not tell, as in an attack, nobody's records were read. The README lists every miss.

Everything you saw runs on synthetic data, and we have not yet measured real customer photos. Banks already warn sellers not to trust payment screenshots. Paid, but nothing arrived? Now you can show the customer where the money stopped. NVIDIA Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory.
